extracted.intended_audience: scientists, science educators, laboratory practitioners, and scientific instrument purchasers (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative remarks about good experimental research practice and science-education materials, plus criteria for judging laboratory instruments and school laboratory courses. Emphasises rigor in method, purity of materials, progressive practical teaching, and instrument performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care and completeness in experimental research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be carried out with elaborate care and completeness; work characterised by thoroughness that is difficult to surpass even with improved apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the overall thoroughness of procedures, extent of experimental detail, and completeness of the investigation; the review cites Marignac's labours as exemplary for their care and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of possible sources of error
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must exercise the greatest care in considering the possibilities of error which might have occurred in operations of previous workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify potential errors in methods and measurements and discuss how they might affect results; the review praises attention to such consideration as a hallmark of reliable work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devising new methods to avoid errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should display ingenuity in devising new methods to avoid known sources of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel methodological adjustments or alternative procedures that reduce systematic or procedural error are valued; Marignac is commended for inventing methods to sidestep earlier workers' pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the purest materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular attention must be paid to employing the purest available materials in experimental work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should check reagent/ sample purity and steps taken to purify materials, since impurities can materially affect fundamental determinations (e.g., atomic weights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat experiments and use multiple independent methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Not satisfied with single runs; whenever practicable adopt repeated experiments on different amounts and two or more independent methods to confirm results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results supported by replication and independent methodological confirmation; the review contrasts single-method results unfavourably with Marignac's multiple-method approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on fundamental and important problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose pressing, foundational problems (e.g., accurate determination of atomic weights) that the field urgently needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value is attached to work that addresses essential data or questions on which other science depends; significance of problem is a criterion for importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive, practical-first course design for school laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: A school laboratory course should be based entirely on practical work, progressive in structure, with later experiments built upon earlier ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a syllabus or course, check that it is hands-on, sequenced so students build skills cumulatively, and that advanced exercises rely on skills learned earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw out students' natural powers and make work interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemata should be devised by teachers skilled at deciding how best to draw out a boy's natural powers and to make his work interesting to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should look for activities that engage curiosity, develop initiative, and are motivating rather than rote; reviewers praise schemes that stimulate student interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for beginners / appropriate difficulty level
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials and experiments should be suitable for beginners (e.g., boys beginning the study), not exceeding their grasp, and accessible to the intended student level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of exposition, required prior knowledge, and whether experiments are manageable by the target students; books praised are 'simply worded' and matched to school level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, intelligibility, and good presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Books and manuals should be clearly and intelligibly written, well supplied with illustrations, with good type and clear printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for plain language, readability, helpful illustrations/diagrams, and quality of typesetting/figures; these features are cited as making texts suitable for school labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and detailed experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental details should be very full and clear, enabling students to carry out and understand the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether procedures include step-by-step instructions, diagrams, reagent quantities, safety notes and explanatory commentary sufficient for novices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of simple questions and exercises to develop ingenuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Value lies in simple questions and exercises proposed for exercising the student's ingenuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coursebooks should include well-designed questions/exercises that prompt problem-solving and application rather than mere copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-arranged syllabus not tied solely to exam requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A good syllabus is well arranged and likely to succeed in schools not tied down to the mere requirements of a syllabus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer syllabi that enable broader understanding and practical skills beyond minimal examination checklists; flexibility and pedagogic coherence are positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact and efficient instrument design (space-saving)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparatus (e.g., condensers) should be compact and efficient, saving bench space while maintaining performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate instruments for physical footprint and whether design innovations (vertical orientation, jackets) preserve or improve performance while saving space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument performance for intended applications (effectiveness with volatiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments must perform effectively for their intended tasks (e.g., condenser must satisfactorily condense volatile substances such as ether, carbon disulphide, acetone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test instruments under representative, challenging conditions and judge whether they achieve complete/adequate performance for typical use-cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and resolving power of optical instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Optical instruments (e.g., student spectroscopes) should have high-quality prisms, precise reading (vernier to single minutes), and be able to resolve diagnostic lines (D lines, sodium lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prism glass quality, scale/readout precision, slit and reflecting prism construction, and actual spectral resolution in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility and adjustability of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments should be adjustable to different tasks (e.g., spectroscope usable for refractive and dispersive power measurements by slight adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer designs that allow adaptation to multiple related measurements with straightforward adjustments, increasing instrument utility in the lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of instruments for laboratory and general work
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments should be suitable for both the laboratory and general work (i.e., robust, reliable, and versatile for educational and research contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate durability, ease of use, and breadth of applications; the student's spectroscope is recommended as 'the best instrument for the laboratory and for all general work in spectrum analysis.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument accuracy and high workmanship standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Meteorological and measurement instruments should be absolutely accurate and of the finest workmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect calibration, materials, and manufacturing quality; accuracy claims should be supported by tests or certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacuum pump performance: guaranteed vacuum level and evacuation speed
rubrics_metrics.description: High-vacuum pumps should achieve and guarantee a specified vacuum (e.g., 0.00004 mm) and evacuate apparatus rapidly (e.g., evacuate a Röntgen tube in 2½ minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both achievable ultimate vacuum and practical pump-down time for realistic loads; guarantees and patent claims should be verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization and certification of measurement tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement tools (e.g., Invar tapes, standard meters) should be standardized and, where relevant, certified by national laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer instruments whose calibration is traceable to national standards (National Physical Laboratory) and that can be supplied with certificates.
